title: Foundations: Labor Anthems - The Complete Guide
summary: What Labor Anthems is, where it came from, and how its songs work.
body:
Labor Anthems songs: Labor anthems are the songs of the union hall: Joe Hill's parodies, Woody Guthrie's dust-bowl ballads, and Pete Seeger's singalongs. They were written to be sung by tired people standing together.

History: The IWW's Little Red Songbook (1909) set hymn tunes to radical words. Guthrie, Seeger, and later Billy Bragg and Utah Phillips kept the tradition: songs as organizing tools.

How the songs work: Labor Anthems favors the keys of G, C, D. Common forms include New words to familiar hymn tunes; Choruses built for group singing. Players should master contrafactum: radical words, hymn melodies first, then the singalong as organizing. Union-hall guitar: simple and loud.

title: Down by the Riverside - Complete Public-Domain Song
summary: Full lyrics and playing guide for Down by the Riverside, a public-domain Labor Anthems standard.
body:
Down by the Riverside (Traditional African-American spiritual, 19th century. Public domain.) is public domain, so this record carries the complete lyrics — sing it, teach it, record it freely.

COMPLETE LYRICS:
Gonna lay down my sword and shield
down by the riverside, down by the riverside, down by the riverside,
gonna lay down my sword and shield
down by the riverside, gonna study war no more.

Chorus:
I ain't gonna study war no more, ain't gonna study war no more,
ain't gonna study war no more.
I ain't gonna study war no more, ain't gonna study war no more,
ain't gonna study war no more.

Gonna put on my long white robe
down by the riverside, down by the riverside, down by the riverside,
gonna put on my long white robe
down by the riverside, gonna study war no more.

Gonna lay down my heavy load
down by the riverside, down by the riverside, down by the riverside,
gonna lay down my heavy load
down by the riverside, gonna study war no more.

HOW TO PLAY IT: a Labor Anthems accompaniment in G using the 'Union I–IV–V' pattern:
G | C | D | G

Technique: contrafactum: radical words, hymn melodies. Union-hall guitar: simple and loud.
